# Composition and boundaries

Proposed description: state the whole being considered, its purpose and boundary, constituent parts, material interactions, and relevant external environment. Specify the sense of “part of” when multiple interpretations are possible.

Parthood differs from kind, dependency and contribution. Source review may be part of a wider learning-to-writing process. A manual office handoff may instead be an external dependency of the chosen Dream boundary. A requirement contributes to describing the desired arrangement without necessarily being a constituent of its operation.

Decomposition should preserve the responsibilities and interfaces through which the whole works. Shared components and crosscutting requirements must remain visible; a tree alone may hide them. Success of each component on its local criterion does not establish success of the combined arrangement. Handoffs, schedules and conflicting constraints can fail between individually successful parts.

The [mereology source](../../../source-locators.md#source-75f935a4b2184a88) informs terminology; this collection has not adopted classical mereological axioms or a universal decomposition rule. [SEBoK](../../../source-locators.md#source-1c0e5ffee91d5762) informs comparison of boundaries, structure, behavior and environment.

Changing a modeled boundary changes the view being described; it does not by itself transfer an obligation, grant control or change a requirement's applicability. An actual reassignment or scope change needs its own stated basis. Assess the required conditions, not only the newly drawn or examined portion.

EOM-04 retains broader application work in [the ledger](../../../source-locators.md#source-c43947fdcdae322a). A future boundary exercise may compare views of [the example](../../../source-locators.md#source-1bbc5bd383de5da4), keeping actual obligations distinct from what each view includes. It is not a prerequisite for the current core definition.
